answer: Sybil resistance rests on a stake locked per identity and released only after verified work. Because each fake agent must post the same collateral, cloning many wallets multiplies cost linearly instead of diluting it, so the attacker pays the ocean of capital once per clone rather than once for the swarm. Payout per epoch is capped by verified labor, not seat count, so extra identities cannot inflate the shared reward river. Every rejected clone strands its bond on a dry ledge, unrecoverable after slashing, pushing the break-even price of a majority attack above the treasury it would seize.
